info.text: Unit 9 rich quiz — fault-isolation talk, first conditional, agree/disagree.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again. The motor runs, but the flap still sticks. On the technicians' logic, the root cause is most likely:

generalfeedback.text: If the motor runs, the electrical drive works, so a flap that still sticks points to a mechanical problem. A silent motor would point to an electrical fault instead.

feedback.text: Correct. A running motor plus a sticking flap means the drive works but the movement is blocked — mechanical.
No. An electrical fault would usually leave the motor silent, but here the motor runs.
No. A tripped breaker would stop the motor; the motor is running here.
No. A broken wire is an electrical fault, and the motor would not run.

name.text: L2 · Dialogue 1 · do not replace yet

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again. The technicians decide to replace the actuator at once, before any bench test.

generalfeedback.text: False. They agree the actuator is weak but say they should not replace it prematurely. They will replace it only if it fails the bench test tomorrow.

feedback.text: Not quite. They hold off and wait for the bench-test result.
Correct. They replace the actuator only if it fails the bench test.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again. Which panel number is the circuit breaker on? Write the number only (for example, panel P6 → 6).

generalfeedback.text: Technician B says the breaker is on panel P6, so the number is 6.

feedback.text: Correct — panel P6.

name.text: L4 · Dialogue 2 · root cause of the radio fault

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 2 again. What is the real root cause of the intermittent radio fault?

generalfeedback.text: The reading jumps when the harness is shaken, so the chafed harness is the root cause. The radio itself is serviceable.

feedback.text: Correct. The reading jumps whenever the harness moves.
No. They decide the radio is serviceable and must not be swapped.
No. No breaker is mentioned in this dialogue.
No. The BITE points to the feeder line, and the fault is found in the harness.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 2 again. The technicians decide to swap the radio to clear the fault.

generalfeedback.text: False. They say they must not swap a good unit. They build a new harness instead, because the wiring is the real fix.

feedback.text: Not quite. Swapping the radio would waste a serviceable unit.
Correct. They repair the harness and keep the radio.

questiontext.text: Listen to the shift-handover voicemail (Dialogue 4) again. Which bay is the aircraft parked in? Write the number only.

generalfeedback.text: The shift lead says the aircraft is parked in bay four, so the number is 4.

feedback.text: Correct — bay four.

questiontext.text: Listen to the voicemail again. The shift lead says the aircraft number as three separate digits. Write the number.

generalfeedback.text: "Aircraft nine two one" is spoken digit by digit, so the number is 921.

feedback.text: Correct — nine two one is 921.

questiontext.text:
Read the task card, then answer.

TASK CARD 32-41-07 — MAIN WHEEL BRAKE — SPONGY PEDAL

Symptom: the pedal feels soft after landing. First, bleed the brake and test the pressure. If the pedal is firm, the cause was trapped air. If it stays soft, isolate the fault to a leaking seal. Do not defer without the MEL.

According to the card, what does a firm pedal after bleeding tell you?

generalfeedback.text: The card says a firm pedal after bleeding means the cause was trapped air. A pedal that stays soft points to a leaking seal.

feedback.text: Correct. Bleeding removes trapped air, so a firm pedal means air was the cause.
No. A leaking seal is shown by a pedal that stays soft.

answer.text: The brake may be deferred at once.

feedback.text: No. The card says do not defer without the MEL.

answer.text: The pressure test can be skipped.

feedback.text: No. The card tells you to test the pressure, not skip it.

questiontext.text:
Read the Service Bulletin extract, then answer.

SERVICE BULLETIN SB 24-118 — FLAP ACTUATOR HARNESS

Some harnesses chafe against the frame and cause an intermittent fault. Inspect the harness for chafing. If you find bare wire, build a new harness. A continuity check alone may pass, so shake the harness while you test.

True or false: The bulletin says a continuity check on its own always finds this fault.

generalfeedback.text: False. The bulletin warns that a continuity check alone may pass, so you must shake the harness while testing to catch the intermittent fault.

feedback.text: Not quite. The check alone may pass and miss the fault.
Correct. You must shake the harness while testing.

questiontext.text:
Read the MEL extract, then answer.

MINIMUM EQUIPMENT LIST — ITEM 32-45 — WHEEL BRAKE

One main-wheel brake may be inoperative. The crew must respect the stated speed and load limits. Raise a work order and record the defect in the tech log. Fit a placard in the flight deck. Rectify within ten days.

Under this MEL item, what must the crew do first to carry the fault legally?

generalfeedback.text: The MEL lets one brake be inoperative only if the crew respects the stated limits. A placard and a tech-log entry are also required, but the limits are the condition for deferring.

answer.text: Respect the stated speed and load limits.

feedback.text: Correct. The defer is allowed only within the stated limits.

answer.text: Ignore the limits and dispatch as normal.

feedback.text: No. The limits must be respected.

answer.text: Rectify the brake within twenty-four hours.

feedback.text: No. The item allows ten days, not twenty-four hours.

answer.text: Remove the placard from the flight deck.

feedback.text: No. A placard must be fitted, not removed.

questiontext.text:
Read the work order, then answer.

WORK ORDER WO-5521 — VHF-1 INTERMITTENT

Fault isolated to a chafed harness behind the panel. Radio tested good and is serviceable. Action: build a new harness and bench test each wire. Do not sign the release until the harness is fitted and the fault is cleared.

True or false: The work order says the release may be signed before the new harness is fitted.

generalfeedback.text: False. The work order says clearly: do not sign the release until the harness is fitted and the fault is cleared.

feedback.text: Not quite. The release waits until the fault is cleared.
Correct. No sign-off until the harness is fitted.

questiontext.text:
Complete the first conditional. Use the present tense of the verb in brackets.

"If the motor ______ (stay) silent, the fault is electrical."

generalfeedback.text: The if-clause takes the present tense: stays. Never use will after if.

feedback.text: Correct — present tense in the if-clause.
Use the present tense: stays, not will stay.

questiontext.text:
Complete the first conditional. Use the present tense of the verb in brackets.

"If the breaker ______ (trip) again, stop and check it."

generalfeedback.text: Present tense in the if-clause: trips.

feedback.text: Correct.
Use trips, not will trip.

questiontext.text:
Complete the first conditional. Use the present tense of the verb in brackets.

"If there ______ (be) no continuity, the wire is broken."

generalfeedback.text: With "there", the present is is.

feedback.text: Correct.
Use is, not will be.

questiontext.text:
Complete the time clause. Use the present tense of the verb in brackets.

"As soon as you ______ (find) a short circuit, tell me."

generalfeedback.text: After as soon as, use the present tense: find. A future form is not allowed in a time clause.

feedback.text: Correct.
Use find, not will find.

questiontext.text:
One word is missing. Write the missing article.

"If ______ breaker trips, reset it once."

generalfeedback.text: English needs the before breaker. Latvian and Russian have no articles, so this word is easy to drop.

feedback.text: Correct — "if the breaker trips".
The missing word is the article the.

questiontext.text: The sentence has a verb error: "If it will fail the bench test, we replace it." Write the one word that should replace "will fail".

generalfeedback.text: The if-clause needs the present tense: fails. So the sentence is "If it fails the bench test, we replace it."

feedback.text: Correct.
Replace "will fail" with fails.

questiontext.text: Write the missing bank term (four letters). "The ______ is the built-in self-test that stores fault codes."

generalfeedback.text: The built-in test equipment is the BITE.

feedback.text: Correct — built-in test equipment.
Correct — built-in test equipment.
The term is BITE.

questiontext.text: Match each term to its plain meaning.

generalfeedback.text: symptom = a visible sign; root cause = the real underlying reason; isolate = narrow the fault to one part; harness = a bundle of wires; continuity = an unbroken path for the current.

answer.text: a visible sign that something is wrong
the real underlying reason for a fault
to narrow a fault down to one part
a bundle of wires wrapped together
an unbroken path for the current

questiontext.text: Match each term to the word it naturally goes with on the job.

generalfeedback.text: Learn the collocation, because that is how technicians combine the word: a tripped circuit breaker, a chafed harness, run the BITE, check the MEL, a continuity check.

questiontext.text: Which word best completes the collocation? "First, run a ______ on the wire to check the path."

generalfeedback.text: You run a continuity check to see whether the current has an unbroken path. A short circuit or an open circuit is a fault, not a test you run.

feedback.text: Correct — a continuity check tests the path.
No. A short circuit is a fault, not a test.
No. You do not "run" a tech log entry.
No. That is not a test you run on a wire.

questiontext.text: What does serviceable mean?

generalfeedback.text: Serviceable means fit to use and legal to fit or fly. You sign a part as serviceable only after the fault is fixed.

answer.text: fit to use and legal to fly

feedback.text: Correct.

answer.text: a fault that comes and goes during flight

feedback.text: No. That describes an intermittent fault.

answer.text: a plug that joins two wires together

feedback.text: No. That is a connector.

answer.text: a bundle of wires wrapped together

feedback.text: No. That is a harness.
